@{6245df8fb4bad813bf989eb1|full_name} Can you share the prompt and large language model you've used for the original post, so that readers can understand your issue more in detail, please?

It seems like a nice idea. But from my experience, several creators I've met are not even aware of the impostor preview being available in avatar details UI. Adding more feature would likely make the user-facing avatar details UI in the VRChat client more complicated for both users & creators, not easier to use. The weighted downsides of additional complexity from this feature request are potentially greater than the plausible benefits from existing methods to test avatars before upload.

Creators are already given the tools to test avatars locally before upload from VRChat SDK - Avatars in Unity. You can also build & test a mobile Toon Standard shaded version of a mobile avatar on Windows, should you not already have a mobile device (a smartphone) available for testing; the only typical difference would be texture compression format (BCn vs ASTC) and texture memory usage (excluding some weirdness from running Android avatar builds on an iOS device, when an iOS built avatar is unavailable).

As for Safety Shield states (e.g. custom animations disabled), you can already preview what an avatar looks like with custom animations disabled, by looking at which GameObjects are disabled/enabled in the Unity hierarchy. VRChat Gesture Manager tool in Unity can help you debug expressions within Unity. Custom shaders disabled in Safety Shield can be tested locally within VRChat from radial hand menu - Options - Avatar - Fallback shaders.

The former two paragraphs I've mentioned practically solve all concerns of "unintended exposure" concerned by an LLM output mostly empty of substance, as long as creators care to test their avatars properly before uploading to VRChat.

Also, this is a duplicated feature request.

- https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/feature-request-separate-cross-platform-avatar-image-previews

Is there something I've missed?

A reminder given your response WubTheCaptain to keep contributions on Canny professional and constructive. While I appreciate the comment regarding AI, the tone and approach you chose detract from the substance of the discussion and make it harder to engage productive conversation to improve VRChat. Also its also worth reiterating the guidance from the tool you referenced: "Our AI detector flags text that may be AI-generated. Use your best judgment when reviewing results. Never rely on AI detection alone to make decisions that could impact someone's career or academic standing."

Since you went through the emotional process of responding in the way you did, I can assume you care about the concerns within this feature request and I will try to restate the issue more clearly and directly for your comprehension.

BLUF:

VRChats current avatar preview does not reliably reflect how an avatar appears across platforms or toggle states, which has led to unintentional and harmful exposure in live instances. Improving preview accuracy would reduce user harm, support creators, and strengthen trust and moderation outcomes.

Driving Problem Statement:

This feature request was prompted by a serious incident involving a minor (15 year old female) who appeared fully nude to others in an instance. The official VRChat client identified her as an Android user, and when the issue was brought to her attention, she was clearly distressed and entirely unaware that this exposure was occurring. From her perspective, what she was showing in the mirror and the avatar preview in the VRChat UI, showed the avatar as fully clothed, offering no indication that anything was wrong.

This is not an isolated occurrence, something that any VRChat user would have seen at least once. I have personally observed similar situations multiple times, often caused by mismatched toggle states, improperly configured menus, or blendshapes that behave differently at runtime than they do in previews. In these cases, users and creators alike lack clear visibility into how an avatar is actually being rendered for others. After discussing this issue with several community members who have seen the same problem, it became clear that this is a recurring platform gap that would make a good feature request.

Proposed Solution:

VRChat should enhance the avatar preview system to accurately reflect all relevant view states, including platform-specific rendering, toggle configurations, and blendshape states. The preview should mirror how avatars are seen in live instances across supported platforms, rather than presenting a single default or idealized view.

Providing this level of visibility would create consistency between what users expect and what others actually see. It would also allow creators another way to catch configuration issues earlier, before avatars are widely distributed or used in public spaces.

Concerns Addressed:

From a trust and safety perspective, this change would significantly reduce the risk of accidental NSFW exposure, whether that involves explicit elements or unintended "ken/barbie" nudity. Clear, accurate previews help users make informed decisions and avoid situations that can cause embarrassment, distress, or risk to the platform.

This consistency also benefits moderation. When preview behavior aligns with runtime behavior, moderators can be more confident that users had a reasonable opportunity to understand how their avatar appeared in an instance, reducing ambiguity during enforcement decisions.

So be it from my firsthand experience, or reinforced by feedback from others in the community, the desire to put stronger, more responsible safegaurds in place was the objective of this feature request. The feature request you referenced is a vague paragraph in 2022 and  not related to this request, I appreciate your attention in trying to find an existing request I was worried I might have missed it.

details:
VRChat should update the Avatar Preview system to accurately represent every render path used on the platform. Today, creators and users cannot reliably see how an avatar appears across PC, Android, iOS, fallback, or protected states, which can result in unintended exposure of NSFW elements or undesirable appearances due to default or toggled configurations. By adding selectable preview modes that mirror each platform and safety state, including shielded/protected views, VRChat can mitigate accidental content exposure, improve user safety, and reduce moderation incidents. This change also empowers creators to identify and fix issues earlier in the pipeline, improving avatar quality and consistency before distribution. Ultimately, aligning the preview with real in-world rendering builds creator trust, improves user experience, and supports safer cross-platform interoperability.

Consistency, Trust, and Creator Support: By aligning menu previews with real runtime behavior, this feature reduces user surprise and moderation risk both in real time and prior to avatar distribution, while giving creators clearer, earlier insight into how their avatars will actually appear across platforms and safety states.
title: Avatar Preview For All Platforms / Viewing Modes
